title: Swiss Glaciers Lose More Ice in 2026
paragraphs: Switzerland's glaciers have endured another punishing year. The latest annual report from the Glacier Monitoring Switzerland network (GLAMOS), published on 1 October, puts the loss in 2026 at more than 5 percent of total ice volume. That falls short of the record set in 2022, but it deepens a longer-term trend: nearly a fifth of the country's glacier ice has gone in just five years.

Two circumstances conspired against the ice. The winter of 2025 and 2026 was among the ten least snowy since measurements began, depriving the glaciers of a protective blanket, and a sweltering summer then pushed the freezing level above 4,000 metres on 76 days, more than twice the usual number and a Swiss record. Between July and September, the glaciers shed roughly 2,200 billion litres of meltwater, over four times the annual drinking-water consumption of Swiss households.

The human-scale casualties are small but symbolic: Bella Tola in Valais and Griessfirn in Glarus have disappeared altogether, while the Rhône, Aletsch and Clariden glaciers recorded their heaviest melt on record. It is worth remembering that this is a monitoring report from one country; it documents the loss with precision but does not attempt to apportion blame among its causes.

questions.q: What phrase suggests that the snowless winter harmed the glaciers?
questions.a: "Depriving the glaciers of a protective blanket".

questions.q: Why does the author call the vanished glaciers "symbolic"?
questions.a: They are small, but their disappearance stands for a larger trend.

questions.q: What does the report not attempt to do?
questions.a: Apportion blame among the causes of the melt.
